comment: Shared by src/shared/ios-sync-merge-contract.test.ts (a reference merge written in the test, until the cards of the three-way merge write the real one in src/shared/ and in LuciumKit) and later by LuciumKit. The three-way merge of docs/synchronisation.md §11. A snapshot is {entities: {kind: {id: {fields, stamps}}}, tombstones: {kind: {id: mark}}, order: {list: [id]}, orderStamps: {list: mark}}; `base: null` is the empty base. `expect` names what must hold: `entities` and `tombstones` are compared whole, `conflicts` whole and in the order (kind, id, field), `order` only for the lists it names. `swap: true` means that merging with local and remote exchanged gives the same entities, tombstones and order, and the same conflicts with every `winner` exchanged. A mark is <13 digits of ms>-<4 hex digits of counter>-<device id>, compared as text; "0" is the mark of a field that was never stamped. Written by a script: the expectations are written by hand and the test runs them.

cases.name: one side changes a field: it is taken
two sides change different fields: both are kept
the same change on both sides is not a conflict (the larger mark is kept)
the same field changed differently: the later mark wins
equal time and counter: the greater device id wins
two values with the same mark (never stamped): the greater canonical text wins
a field removed on one side and untouched on the other: removed (its mark stays)
a field removed on one side and changed on the other: the later mark wins
an entity added on one side only is kept
two different entities added on the two sides: the union
the same id added on both sides: merged field by field from an empty base
deleted on one side, untouched on the other: deleted
deleted on one side, modified on the other: kept, the deletion loses
deleted on both sides: stays deleted, the larger tombstone mark is kept
a folder deleted on one side while a tab moves into it on the other: the folder is kept
a space deleted with its tabs on one side, untouched on the other: all deleted
a tab left in a deleted space is removed and leaves a tombstone (reference repair)
a dangling folder reference is cleared (the tab goes to the root)
folders that would form a cycle: the parent of the smallest id is cleared
unknown fields and unknown kinds go through
an unknown field changed on both sides is a conflict like any other
a setting is one register
order: nobody reorders and each side adds: the additions go to the end by birth mark, then id
order: one side reorders, the other adds: the reordered list is kept, the addition goes to the end
order: both reorder: the later mark wins and what the other side added goes to the end
order: a deleted member leaves the list
first synchronisation (empty base): the union, a conflict is settled by the mark
empty base: a change newer than the tombstone brings the entity back
empty base: a tombstone newer than every change deletes the entity
a space set aside on one side is left out on both sides, with what depends on it
merging a snapshot with itself changes nothing (idempotence)
